note_ja: 禅寺の精進料理と浄土真宗の報恩講の膳が重なり、町ごとの豆腐屋が厚手の揚げを作り続けてきた土地とされる
note_en: Where Zen temple cooking and the memorial feasts of Jodo Shinshu temples overlap, and neighborhood tofu makers are said to have kept frying thick-cut aburaage.

note_ja: 山あいの門前町で、串に刺して油を切る厚く大きな揚げが参拝客や市の客に供されてきたと伝わる土地
note_en: A mountain temple town where thick, oversized sheets, speared on skewers to drain, are said to have been served to pilgrims and market-goers.

note_ja: 軟水の地下水と寺院の精進料理に支えられた豆腐屋の集積が、だしを含ませる薄く大判の揚げを育てたとされる土地
note_en: Soft groundwater and temple vegetarian cooking are said to have concentrated tofu makers here and bred the thin, wide sheet that drinks up dashi.

note_ja: 山上の寺院と宿坊の精進料理が、冬に凍った豆腐を保存食に仕立てる工夫を育てたと伝わる土地
note_en: The mountaintop temples and pilgrim lodgings whose vegetarian cooking is said to have turned winter-frozen tofu into a storable food.

note_ja: 冷え込みの厳しい内陸の冬を利用して豆腐を凍らせ乾かす凍り豆腐の産地とされる
note_en: An inland prefecture whose hard winters are said to have made it a center of kori-dofu, tofu frozen and dried in the cold.

note_ja: 吾妻おろしの寒風で豆腐を凍らせ乾かす凍み豆腐づくりが農閑期の仕事として続く土地
note_en: Where the Azuma-oroshi winter wind is used to freeze and dry tofu, a task of the farming off-season that continues today.

note_ja: 禅寺の精進料理の需要と豆乳の味を決める軟水の地下水が重なり、寺の門前に湯葉屋が集まってきたとされる土地
note_en: Where the demand of Zen temple kitchens met soft groundwater that shapes the taste of soy milk, drawing yuba makers to the temple gates.

note_ja: 日光山の修行僧の膳から広まり、二つ折りで厚みを出す湯波や揚げ巻き湯波が社寺の供え膳と家庭に根づいたとされる土地
note_en: Where yuba spread from the tables of Mount Nikko's monks, and thick double-folded sheets and fried rolls took root in shrine offerings and home cooking.

note_ja: 身延山の僧を支える精進の食として伝わり、町内の複数の製造元が厚みの異なる生湯葉を作り分ける土地
note_en: Where fresh yuba is said to have begun as food for the monks of Mount Minobu, and several makers in town still produce sheets of differing thickness.
